title: Rust: Enums and Pattern Matching
description: Work with Rust enums (sum types) and exhaustive pattern matching.

steps.title: Simple Enum
steps.description: Define an enum `Direction` with variants `North`, `South`, `East`, `West`. Write a function `describe(d: Direction) -> &str` that returns the direction name for each variant.
hints: Match must be exhaustive (cover all variants).

steps.title: Enum with Data
steps.description: Define an enum `Shape` with variants `Circle(f64)`, `Rectangle(f64, f64)`, `Triangle(f64, f64)`. Implement an `area(&self) -> f64` method for each.

verification.failureMessage: Print area of Circle(5), Rectangle(4,5), Triangle(3,4).

steps.title: Option and Some/None
steps.description: Write a function `safe_index(vec: &[i32], index: usize) -> Option<&i32>` that returns `Some(value)` if index is in bounds, or `None` otherwise. Test with valid and invalid indices.
hints: Print the value or 'Index out of bounds'.

steps.title: Nested Enums
steps.description: Define `enum WebEvent { WantsToQuit, KeyPress(char), Click { x: i64, y: i64 }, Paste(String) }`. Write a function `inspect(event: WebEvent)` that prints details for each variant.
hints: Match each variant with its associated data.

verification.failureMessage: Print details for each WebEvent variant.

steps.title: Enum with if let
steps.description: Using the `Shape` enum, use `if let Circle(r) = shape` to match a single variant without a full match. Print the radius if it's a Circle, otherwise print 'Not a circle'.
hints: `if let Circle(r) = shape { println!("Radius: {}", r); } else { println!("Not a circle"); }`
`if let` is concise for single-arm pattern matching.
Test with both a Circle and a Rectangle.

verification.failureMessage: Print radius for Circle and 'Not a circle' for Rectangle.
